subject: Draft case study: cost & efficiency story — review and redlines
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Barnes <oliver@harborlogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft case study: cost & efficiency story — review and redlines

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for the great conversation last week. Per our plan, attached is a first-pass draft of the customer story that highlights the pipeline, latency, and cost savings you achieved after moving inference to Redwood Dedicated. We focused the narrative on a single pilot pod and the month-over-month savings to keep the story tight.

A few asks from our side:
- Can you review the numbers in the "Results" section for accuracy (particularly the 48% cost figure and the "<24ms median latency" line)?
- Are there any technical details you want omitted for confidentiality (team names, internal tool names)?
- Legal will likely ask for an anonymized revenue impact statement rather than exact revenue. If you prefer ranges or percentages, pls flag it.

I’ve also shared the live doc here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcDeFg_case_study_draft_v2 (editable for comments). Attachment: case_study_draft_v1.docx.

If easier, we can schedule a 30-minute redline session this week — happy to coordinate.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0128

--
Attachment: case_study_draft_v1.docx (Microsoft Word doc, 46 KB)

From: Oliver Barnes <oliver@harborlogistics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Review <legal@harborlogistics.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Draft case study: cost & efficiency story — review and redlines

Neha —

Thanks for sending this over. We appreciate the draft; overall it reads well. I attached our annotated PDF with inline redlines and a few comments: harbor_redlines_20261109.pdf. Main items from our side: 

1) Numbers: please change the headline 48% to "~45% (pilot average)" — we can’t commit to the exact 48% across all clusters.
2) Anonymization: remove all mentions of internal team names ("OpsTeam-A") and any internal tool references.
3) Customer contacts: please replace personal names with titles (e.g., "Head of Infrastructure") in quotes unless we've signed off on named attribution.
4) Revenue impacts: Legal prefers a qualitative phrasing or a range ("mid-single-digit to low-double-digit percentage uplift in operational throughput").

We’ll run a quick legal check but wanted to get these primary redlines back to you now. Happy to join a call — I’m available Thursday morning eastern.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: Draft case study: cost & efficiency story — review and redlines

Quick internal summary and suggested approach: 

- Customer asks: soften the 48% claim to ~45% pilot average; anonymize team names; avoid PII and revenue specifics. Legal will follow up with a one-page checklist.
- Recommended edits before sending v2 to customer:
  * Change all hard numbers in headline to ranges or "~45%"
  * Replace quoted names with titles and ask for explicit named approval if we want attribution
  * Move detailed latency distribution table to an appendix (or remove) — keeps headline focused

Action items for us: 
1) Neha — prepare v2 with the above changes and attach a clean copy and a tracked-changes doc for the customer.
2) Stephanie — can you run the compliance checklist and flag any items that require engineering confirmation (e.g., exact sequence length used in benchmark)?
3) Marissa — I’ll prep a short talking points doc for the redline call (if we set one).

If Neha can get v2 to Oliver by EOD Wednesday (PST), we stand a good chance of legal doing a light review and returning approval by Monday.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Marketing | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Oliver —

Thanks for the quick review and the annotated PDF. I incorporated your primary asks and attached v2 (case_study_draft_v2.docx). Key changes:
- Headline adjusted to "~45% pilot-average reduction in inference unit cost" (moved 48% to an appendix note with source data).
- Removed internal team names and replaced personal quotes with titles where possible. I flagged one quote where you might prefer the original phrasing — see comment in the doc.
- Reworded revenue impact to a qualitative range per your legal note.

Attachment: case_study_draft_v2.docx (with tracked changes). I also added a one-page appendix that shows the benchmark parameters (sequence length, batch size) in case engineering wants to confirm. Stephanie — can you confirm the appendix accuracy?

If it helps, I scheduled a 30-minute call for Thu 12 Nov at 10:00 AM ET (placeholder) — let me know if that works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Neha

For now: you have our provisional approval to proceed with Redwood's usual press/marketing cadence once the appendix label is added and legal confirms. Attached: approved-stamp.png for internal use once final signoff is received.

Thanks for moving quickly on this — please send the final cleaned copy after the appendix label change and we’ll return the legal signoff.
